verdicts.reason: A rearranges properly for the square (headline and copy on top, product, CTA), but the legal line is moved up under the subhead, so it sits above the product, too large and out of reading order, and the headline's 'last' runs into the pale circle. B keeps the original order, but the subhead, legal and CTA are packed into the bottom third with almost no gap above the button, and a bubble sits on '2026' in the legal line ('20⊙6'), which is a real text collision.

A's split layout breaks the headline onto three lines with an orphaned 'last'. The ribbon and logo are a scattered, misaligned pair at the top right, the legal text is a three-line block that competes with the subhead, and there are dead areas at the upper left and lower right, with the product resting on the dark circle. B has a coherent centred stack, but the copy is cramped above the CTA and a bubble collides with '2026' in the legal line.

B is the portrait original shrunk into a narrow centre column: wide empty side margins, a small CTA, and legal text so tiny it is unreadable at this size, so it is not a real rearrangement. A uses the square width with a full-width headline and a large CTA, but the bottom text stack is cramped and a bubble overlaps '2026' in the legal line.

A is the original shrunk into a centred column: the legal text is unreadably small, the CTA and headline are undersized, and big empty bands sit on both sides. B rearranges for the square with a strong headline and CTA, but the headline nearly touches the side edges (thin margins), overlaps the pale circle, and the legal line is promoted above the product, too large and out of reading order.
